newsitem.title: UK: Morgan Crucible says expects good 1997.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Crucible says expects good 1997.

text.p: Morgan Crucible Co Plc, the UK specialised industrial chemicals and services group, said it expects another good year despite difficult trading conditions.

"Market conditions are not easy, but we are not dependent on a single economy or industry and look forward to another good year for Morgan," managing director Bruce Farmer said in a statement accompanying its annual results.

Pretax profits before exceptional items were up 15.2 percent at 98.0 million stg in the year to January 4, 1997, against 85.1 million the year before. Profits including exceptional items rose 17.9 percent to 100.2 million stg against 85.0 million.

"The investments we have made over recent years in broadening Morgan Crucible's product portfolio within its core divisions, together with the widening of its geographical base, are producing good results for shareholders," Farmer said.

Headline earnings per share were up 15.5 percent at 29.1 pence versus 25.2 pence the year before on turnover of 897.5 million stg against 847.8 million. Acquisitions contributed 32 million stg to this year's turnover.
"Morgan had a good year against a background of difficult trading conditions," the company said in a statement.

Southeast Asia and North America showed the strongest growth but this was restricted in the first half in North America owing to disputes in the automotive industry and downturns in parts of the electronics and defence sectors.
Conditions in the UK were mixed, while continental Europe suffered in the absence of economic recovery in Germany and France.
"The strength of Morgan's geographic and market spread and its organic growth capability were most apparent in these circumstances," the company added.
It said all its divisions increased sales, profits and margins over the previous year.
